title: Carthage holds: the Western Empire keeps Africa
divergence: In 439 the Vandal attack on Carthage fails and the western government keeps the African provinces.
geographic_scope: Western Mediterranean: Italy, Africa, Gaul, Hispania; the eastern empire follows its real course
constraints: Only one divergence: the Vandal capture of Carthage in 439 does not happen.
Everything before 439 is real history and cites dossier claims.
The eastern empire keeps its documented history unless a western event plausibly changes it.
No quantities without sources; outcomes are described qualitatively.
assumptions: African tax revenue and grain were central to the western state's finances (dossier c_vandal_grain, c_annona).
A western state with revenue can keep paying its army and court, so the 476 coup is not inevitable.
Roman engineering traditions (aqueducts, water mills, domed architecture) continue where the state keeps funding them.

events.title: Carthage resists the Vandals
events.description: The Vandal assault on Carthage fails. The western government keeps the African provinces and their port.

events.title: African grain keeps sailing to Rome
events.description: Taxes in kind and the state grain shipments from Africa to Rome continue.

events.title: No coup in Italy
events.description: With its revenue intact, the western court keeps paying its army, and Odoacer's deposition of the emperor does not happen.

events.title: Water power spreads
events.description: State-funded engineering continues and aqueduct-fed water mills of the Barbegal type are built in more cities.

events.title: Domes in the West
events.description: Western cities build large domed churches on the model of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.
